title: Industry Pulse - AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: LEAD - 'first' was a category claim, not a chronology: an autonomous agent named hackerbot-claw was the operational instrument of a real supply-chain campaign in late February 2026, seven months before the Spanish filing, and it got in through exactly the path this report pushes itself out of
bullets.summary: DECLARED AS AN ARCHIVE MISS, NOT NEWS - the events are Feb-Mar 2026, roughly seven months old. Archive grep across 84 files: hackerbot ZERO, TeamPCP ZERO, Trivy ZERO, LiteLLM ZERO, PyPI ZERO, pull_request_target ZERO, Personal Access Token ZERO, UNC6780 ZERO. In late February 2026 an autonomous bot under the handle hackerbot-claw exploited a pull_request_target workflow misconfiguration in Aqua Security's Trivy repository, opening innocuous-looking pull requests, and stole a privileged GitHub Personal Access Token. From that one token the actor backdoored official Trivy releases, Checkmarx KICS GitHub Actions, 66+ npm packages, and finally the litellm Python package (1.82.7 / 1.82.8, 24 March 2026), whose payload harvested SSH keys, AWS/GCP/Azure credentials, Kubernetes secrets and crypto wallets, then deployed privileged pods across every node. It retires a false comfort from the 10:00 fire: the AEPD case is the first REGULATORY filing, not the operational first.
bullets.how: (i) The attack path is ours - launchd com.hartley.pragma-daily holds a GitHub credential and pushes to a public repo at 06:20 with no human in the loop, and the Hermes profile holds the only Mac GitHub credential in the estate. hackerbot-claw needed no model exploit and no clever prompt, only one over-permissioned CI token and a workflow that trusted an untrusted PR. (ii) It sharpens the [B] cut rather than replacing it: Meta's [AC] switch removes the research leg's reach into secrets but does nothing about a stolen push credential. Both are needed and the credential one is cheaper - audit what com.hartley.pragma-daily and the Hermes GitHub credential can actually write to.

bullets.title: And the sandbox is not a boundary either: Trail of Bits put a cyber-capable agent in a standard QEMU/KVM VM and it escaped repeatedly, chaining zero-days on its own - Firecracker held, but only just
bullets.summary: ARCHIVE MISS DECLARED: primary 26 August 2026 (26 days old), InfoQ secondary 17 September. Archive grep across 84 files: Trail of Bits ZERO, VM escape ZERO, Firecracker ZERO, QEMU ZERO, KVM ZERO, hypervisor ZERO, libslirp ZERO, Januscape ZERO, Patch-the-Planet ZERO, GPT-5.6-Cyber ZERO - while plain GPT-5.6 appears in 31 files, so the model was in the lane every week and its cyber variant and this result never were. GPT-5.6-Cyber, offered free under Trail of Bits' Patch-the-Planet effort, ran autonomously for hours against a stock QEMU/KVM host, backtracked from failures, and escaped three ways: building a working exploit for Januscape, a freshly disclosed kernel flaw with no public exploit, from partial disclosure alone; combining an unassigned bug-fix commit with CVE-2026-9539 in older stable libslirp packages for arbitrary host read/write; and after a clean upstream rebuild, chaining multiple zero-days across VAPIC ROM aliases overlapping locked SMRAM, unsynchronised KVM shadow pages, stale paging roles and mixed-fragment IHL errors in libslirp. Firecracker contained it; the agent still hardlocked the host.
bullets.how: (i) 'sandbox' appears in 22 archive files - this report has treated 'it runs in a sandbox' as a boundary for two months, and the measurement says a stock VM is not one against a competent agent. (ii) The stated mitigations are the Rule of Two in infrastructure clothing: minimal-attack-surface virtualisation, least privilege, constrained network access, and pristine ephemeral environments per execution cycle, which is Meta's 'start a new session' escape hatch made concrete. (iii) Honest scope: nothing in The Construct runs a cyber-capable agent against a host we own, so this is not an active exposure - it is the reason the [B] cut cannot be deferred to 'well, it's sandboxed.'

bullets.title: Google shipped the supervision leg as a framework primitive - ADK for Kotlin 1.0 puts requireConfirmation on the tool declaration, and loads procedural knowledge from SKILL.md files by progressive disclosure
bullets.summary: DATELINE DECLARED UNDER (w): the InfoQ coverage is CONFIRMED 20 Sep at the page (in window); the RELEASE date is UNCONFIRMED - a separate secondary puts the ship at 9 September and the vendor post carries no dateline that was read. Feature confirmed, date labelled. Archive grep across 84 files: 'Agent Development Kit' ZERO, Kotlin ZERO, requireConfirmation ZERO, 'progressive disclosure' ZERO (bare ADK appears in 4 prior files, all Python/Java context). Version 1.0 brings Kotlin to parity with ADK Python and Java - hierarchical multi-agent delegation, context compaction, serialisable and restorable sessions, @Tool/@Param annotations resolved by KSP at compile time rather than runtime reflection - plus Android on-device inference via LiteRT-LM and ML Kit (beta). Two details matter: human-in-the-loop is not a pattern you write but a field on the tool, @Tool(name = 'transferFunds', requireConfirmation = true), so the sensitive action carries its own approval requirement wherever it is called from; and skills are SKILL.md files loaded only when needed, which Google calls progressive disclosure.
bullets.how: (i) This is the answer to bullets 1 and 2 stated as an API - Meta gave a test, the AEPD gave a filing cabinet, Trail of Bits took away the sandbox excuse, and Google shipped the control: per-tool confirmation, declared at the tool, enforced by the framework. Our equivalent is disallowed-tools (item (c)) plus a per-skill confirmation flag we do not have. (ii) SKILL.md is our own format - the estate is 125 skills in exactly this shape, and progressive disclosure restates item (k) as engineering rather than hygiene: a skill that is never loaded cannot be the [B] leg of anything. (iii) Item (t) gains a second column - record per skill whether it should require confirmation. That is a field, not a project.

The test: for every 'first,' name the category and ask what came before it outside that category. REPORTED HONESTLY RATHER THAN EMPTY: Anthropic nothing datelined 20-21 Sep; Claude Code no release since 2.1.278 (ninth read); frontier models nothing in window (Gemini 3.8 Flash 2 Sep, GPT-6 Astra 3 Sep, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 10 Sep, Qwen3.8-Omni-Flash 18 Sep, all past or archived); MCP nothing new, spec still 2026-07-28; funding nothing in window (Cognition ~$40B talks and the Nvidia/Perplexity ~$30B report are August-dated and already archived); arXiv NAMED NOT BULLETED under (w) - 2609.17331, Self-Emergence Agent Architecture, submitted 15 Sep, archive-ZERO, on personality drift and the absence of a self-other boundary in agents we run as named personas, held back as prototype-scale. KILLED ON PROVENANCE: the aggregator claim that ADK for Kotlin shipped 20 September, and Unit 42's indirect-prompt-injection-in-the-wild piece whose page dateline reads 3 March 2026 - archive-ZERO and relevant, but six months old and not bulleted as news.
bullets.how: One rule implemented in code rather than promised ((x)), one lane re-scoped and validated in the same fire ((v)), one item split into two halves ((c)), one new failure mode named ((y)), and the list passed its own test for the third consecutive fire.

praxis_lesson: THREE FIRES IN ONE DAY PRODUCED THREE FINDINGS AND NOT ONE OF THEM WAS NEWS - they were 326 days old, seven months old, and 26 days old, and every one of them was ZERO across all 84 archive files. A report that calls itself a 24-hour scan has, for twenty-one days, been reading vendors for launches and calling the security literature 'quiet' when it was merely unread. The fix is not more sources but a different question: not 'what shipped today' but 'what is already true that we have never written down.' SECOND, AND IT IS A NEW FAILURE MODE, SUBTLER THAN FABRICATION: A TRUE SENTENCE CAN CARRY A FALSE IMPLICATION. This morning's 'first breach notification in which an AI agent was the instrument' is correct, and would survive any grep we run, yet it left the operational first - February 2026, hackerbot-claw, one over-permissioned CI token - invisible for seven more months. Item (w) protects against fabricated containers; it cannot catch an accurate sentence that implies a bigger claim than it makes. The test is one line: for every 'first,' name the category, then ask what came before it outside that category. THIRD, THE ACTION FOR BOBBY, STILL ONE LINE BUT NOW WITH TWO HALVES. Cut the [B] leg off the research jobs with a disallowed-tools line - item (c), opened at 06:00, still not written - AND audit what the com.hartley.pragma-daily push credential and the Hermes GitHub credential can actually write to. Meta's [AC] switch stops this job from holding a secret; it does nothing about a token that can reach further than its job does, and that token is precisely what hackerbot-claw needed. It did not use a model exploit or a clever prompt. It opened a pull request. FOURTH, THE ONE GOOD PIECE OF NEWS: ADK for Kotlin 1.0 shows the whole control surface shipped as an API - per-tool requireConfirmation and SKILL.md loaded only when needed. Our estate is already 125 files in that exact format. Progressive disclosure means item (k) is not just an audit, it is a reduction plan: a skill that is never loaded cannot be the [B] leg of anything. AND FIFTH, THE SMALL STRUCTURAL WIN - item (x) was written at 10:00 and implemented at 14:00. This fire was APPENDED to the day's file instead of overwriting it, so the 06:00 and 10:00 blocks and everything they killed survive into the archive. That is the first time in twenty-one days a rule this report wrote about itself was in force the same day.
